hints.title: Decoupling the Ride Choices
hints.text: For an ordering where land is completed first, the earlier the land ride finishes, the earlier any subsequent water ride can start.

hints.title: Optimal First Ride
hints.text: Identify the absolute earliest finish time among all first-choice rides in a single linear pass.

hints.title: Linear Scan of Successor
hints.text: Feed this optimal transition time into each candidate second ride and pick the overall minimum finish time.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def earliestFinishTime(self, landStartTime: List[int], landDuration: List[int], waterStartTime: List[int], waterDuration: List[int]) -> int:
        # Minimum completion time for land alone
        min_l_finish = min(s + d for s, d in zip(landStartTime, landDuration))
        # Minimum completion time for water alone
        min_w_finish = min(s + d for s, d in zip(waterStartTime, waterDuration))
        
        # Land first, then water
        best_lw = min(max(min_l_finish, ws) + wd for ws, wd in zip(waterStartTime, waterDuration))
        # Water first, then land
        best_wl = min(max(min_w_finish, ls) + ld for ls, ld in zip(landStartTime, landDuration))
        
        return min(best_lw, best_wl)
```

complexity.notes: Reduces quadratic pair checking to two independent linear scans.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(N * M) checking exceeds time limits when N and M reach 100,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Accumulates prefix minimums on the fly using constant auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Notice that the initial stage choice is monotonic with respect to the successor start time.
